D.t: Jermaine Johnson trails by 6.9 and wins 15% of simulations. Closing it takes about 70,049 voters switching sides, or 140,098 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +15.4 and D +1.9. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +10.7. Your best recent poll is New York Times/Siena at R +7.7; your worst is Trafalgar Group (R) at R +14.9. 8 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Richland, a projected net 61,341 votes; Charleston, a projected net 22,219 votes; Orangeburg, a projected net 10,132 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: York, R +4.3, 5.7% of the vote; Berkeley, R +3.5, 4.3% of the vote; Beaufort, R +5.8, 4.1% of the vote; Dorchester, R +1.3, 3.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Jermaine Johnson runs furthest behind in Richland, Greenville, Florence. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 66% of voters, 45 to 52, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.28 points; Voters without a degree, 62% of voters, 47 to 50, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.09 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 60% of voters, 48 to 49, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.99 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Jermaine Johnson: Immigration voters 15 to 82, White voters 36 to 61, Men 40 to 57. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$136K cash against $1.7M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.2 points away from Jermaine Johnson. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
Cash: $1.7M in the bank against $136K for Jermaine Johnson.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Horry, a projected net 37,467 votes; Greenville, a projected net 34,139 votes; Lexington, a projected net 29,630 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: York, R +4.3, 5.7% of the vote; Berkeley, R +3.5, 4.3% of the vote; Beaufort, R +5.8, 4.1% of the vote; Dorchester, R +1.3, 3.0% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Alan Wilson runs furthest behind in Greenwood, York, Horry. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 66% of voters, 52 to 45, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.28 points; Voters without a degree, 62% of voters, 50 to 47, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.09 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 60% of voters, 49 to 48, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.99 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Alan Wilson: Black voters 19 to 78, Independents 25 to 69, Moderates 33 to 63. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$1.7M cash against $136K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
